missions.title: The Materials Investigation
missions.story: The science workshop received mixed-up samples and test records. Learners identify material changes, separate useful mixtures and investigate living systems.
missions.focus: Physical/chemical change; mixtures; separation and fair tests; circulation and plant reproduction.

finalChallenge.title: Solve the Workshop Case
finalChallenge.description: Solve the workshop case: classify changes and mixtures, choose separation methods, and plan a fair greenhouse investigation.

steps.prompt: Solve the Workshop Case: classify these observations as Physical Change or Chemical Change.
items: Melting wax into liquid form
Rust forming on an iron fixture
Dissolving sugar crystals into warm tea
Baking dough into bread (releasing gases and aroma)
steps.success: Changes classified with scientific evidence!

steps.prompt: How can you separate a mixture of sand and saltwater to collect both dry sand and dry salt?
items: Freeze the mixture until it turns into glass
Filter the mixture to remove sand, then evaporate the water to recover salt crystals
Use a magnet on the water
steps.success: Mission 1 complete! You earned the Materials Investigator Badge!

checkpoints.title: Changes and Mixtures Lab
checkpoints.npcOpening: Welcome to Changes and Mixtures Lab! Study the clue first, try the activity, and answer the questions to earn your reward.
checkpoints.lesson: A physical change may affect shape, size or state without forming a new substance; some changes are reversible. A chemical change forms new substances. Mixtures contain substances combined physically. Uniform mixtures appear evenly mixed; non-uniform mixtures have visibly different parts. A substance may change state by gaining or losing heat.

miniGame.name: Sample Sort
miniGame.instructions: Sort melting ice, tearing paper, rusting iron and sand mixed with pebbles.

steps.prompt: Sample Sort: classify each change as Physical Change or Chemical Change.
items: Ice melting into liquid water
An iron nail developing reddish rust
Tearing a sheet of paper into small pieces
Wood burning into ash and smoke
steps.success: Spot on! Chemical changes form new substances, physical changes alter form without new substances.

steps.prompt: Mixture Analysis: classify these mixtures as Uniform (Homogeneous) or Non-Uniform (Heterogeneous).
items: Salt completely dissolved in clear water
Pebbles mixed with dry rice grains
Filtered sugar dissolved in warm water
Vegetable oil floating on water
steps.success: Uniform solutions appear identical throughout; non-uniform mixtures have visibly distinct parts.

questions.text: Which example is mainly a physical change?
questions.explanation: Melting changes water’s state without creating a new substance.
questions.feedback: Melting changes water’s state without creating a new substance.

questions.text: Which observation strongly indicates a new substance formed?
options: Water being poured into a bowl
questions.explanation: Rust is a new material produced by a chemical reaction.
questions.feedback: Rust is a new material produced by a chemical reaction.

questions.text: Which mixture is usually uniform after stirring until all the salt dissolves?
questions.explanation: A dissolved salt solution looks uniform throughout.
questions.feedback: A dissolved salt solution looks uniform throughout.

questions.text: Which mixture is non-uniform?
questions.explanation: Rice and pebbles remain visibly distinct components.
questions.feedback: Rice and pebbles remain visibly distinct components.

questions.text: Which flow best represents freezing?
questions.explanation: Cooling liquid water can make it solidify into ice.
questions.feedback: Cooling liquid water can make it solidify into ice.

checkpoints.title: Separation & Fair Test Workshop
checkpoints.npcOpening: Welcome to Separation & Fair Test Workshop! Study the clue first, try the activity, and answer the questions to earn your reward.
checkpoints.lesson: Sieving separates larger solid particles from smaller ones. Filtration can separate an insoluble solid from a liquid, and evaporation can recover a dissolved solid from solution. A fair test changes one variable while controlling other important factors. Repeating trials improves confidence in the result.

miniGame.name: Separation Route
miniGame.instructions: Choose sieving, filtration or evaporation for three sample mixtures; identify controls.

steps.prompt: Separation Route: choose the most effective separation method for each mixture.
items: Separating large pebbles from fine sand
Separating insoluble sand from water
Recovering dissolved salt from saltwater
Trapping tea leaves from brewed tea liquid
steps.success: Great lab technique! Sieving uses pore size, filtration traps solids, evaporation removes liquid.

questions.text: Which method is best for separating sand from water?
questions.explanation: A filter can trap the sand while water passes through.
questions.feedback: A filter can trap the sand while water passes through.

questions.text: How can pebbles be separated from fine sand?
questions.explanation: A sieve lets smaller sand particles pass while keeping larger pebbles.
questions.feedback: A sieve lets smaller sand particles pass while keeping larger pebbles.

questions.text: Which method can recover dissolved salt from saltwater?
options: Using a sieve for the solution
Collecting the salt with a magnet
questions.explanation: Removing water by evaporation leaves dissolved salt behind.
questions.feedback: Removing water by evaporation leaves dissolved salt behind.

questions.text: A student tests sugar dissolving in warm and cool water. Which should be kept the same?
options: The amount of sugar and volume of water
questions.explanation: Only temperature should change in the intended fair comparison.
questions.feedback: Only temperature should change in the intended fair comparison.

questions.text: Why should scientific experiments be repeated?
options: To make the answer always the same
To check whether results are consistent
questions.explanation: Multiple trials help evaluate repeatability and reliability.
questions.feedback: Multiple trials help evaluate repeatability and reliability.

checkpoints.title: Living Systems Greenhouse
checkpoints.npcOpening: Welcome to Living Systems Greenhouse! Study the clue first, try the activity, and answer the questions to earn your reward.
checkpoints.lesson: The heart pumps blood through blood vessels. Blood carries oxygen and nutrients to body cells. Plants may reproduce through seeds or, for some plants, vegetative methods such as cuttings. A fair plant investigation compares methods using similar soil, light and watering conditions.

miniGame.name: Greenhouse Helper
miniGame.instructions: Connect heart to blood vessel diagram and sort seed-growing versus cutting propagation.

steps.prompt: What is the primary role of the heart in the circulatory system?
items: Filtering oxygen directly from air into stomach
Pumping blood through blood vessels to supply oxygen and nutrients
Digesting solid food into glucose
steps.success: The heart acts as a muscular pump driving the circulatory system.

steps.prompt: Greenhouse Helper: classify plant reproduction methods as Sexual (Seeds) or Asexual (Vegetative).
items: Growing a mango tree from a seed
Propagating a rose bush from a stem cutting
Growing a new sweet potato from a tuber
Flowering plant pollinated to develop seed pods
steps.success: Clear distinction! Seeds involve sexual reproduction; cuttings and tubers reproduce vegetatively.

questions.text: What is the main job of the heart in the circulatory system?
options: Carry air into the lungs directly
questions.explanation: The heart pumps blood through blood vessels.
questions.feedback: The heart pumps blood through blood vessels.

questions.text: Which substance is transported by blood to body cells?
questions.explanation: Blood carries oxygen obtained through respiration to cells.
questions.feedback: Blood carries oxygen obtained through respiration to cells.

questions.text: What is one way a plant can reproduce without a seed?
questions.explanation: Some plants can develop into new plants from stem cuttings.
questions.feedback: Some plants can develop into new plants from stem cuttings.

questions.text: What should stay the same when comparing two plant-growing methods fairly?
questions.explanation: Keeping environmental conditions similar isolates the growing method.
questions.feedback: Keeping environmental conditions similar isolates the growing method.

questions.text: Which evidence would best show that a cutting developed into a new plant?
options: The old stem became dry immediately
It formed roots and new leaves
questions.explanation: Roots and new leaves indicate active growth.
questions.feedback: Roots and new leaves indicate active growth.

missions.title: The Ecosystem Engineering Quest
missions.story: A river habitat needs repair, and a village workshop needs a device to lift supplies. Students combine ecosystem reasoning with engineering and wave observations.
missions.focus: Food webs and ecological roles; biotic/abiotic interactions; simple machines, fair tests and water/sound waves.

finalChallenge.title: Restore Balance
finalChallenge.description: Restore balance: build a food web, identify a possible habitat problem using evidence, and choose a practical simple machine based on tests.

steps.prompt: Restore Balance: arrange the forest ecosystem food chain in order of energy transfer.
items: Forest Ferns & Plants (Producers)
Herbivorous Deer (Primary Consumer)
Wolf Pack (Secondary Predator)
Fungi & Microbes (Decomposers)
steps.success: Ecosystem balance restored!

steps.prompt: Which simple machine would require the least effort force to lift a 100 kg generator into a clinic?
items: Lifting it straight up with bare hands
Using a gentle, low-angle inclined plane ramp with rollers
Dropping it from a roof
steps.success: Mission 2 complete! You earned the Ecosystem Engineer Badge!

checkpoints.title: Food Web Forest
checkpoints.npcOpening: Welcome to Food Web Forest! Study the clue first, try the activity, and answer the questions to earn your reward.
checkpoints.lesson: Plants are producers because they make their own food. Consumers eat other organisms; decomposers break down dead matter. Scavengers feed on dead animals. Food chains and food webs show who eats whom, with arrows showing the direction of energy transfer. Removing one organism can affect others.

miniGame.name: Food Web Builder
miniGame.instructions: Connect grass → grasshopper → frog → snake and add decomposers.

steps.prompt: Food Web Builder: classify the organisms by their ecological role in the ecosystem.
items: Green grass producing food by photosynthesis
Grasshopper feeding on plant leaves
Mushroom fungus decomposing dead wood
Vulture feeding on dead animal remains
Snake hunting frogs
steps.success: Producers make food, consumers feed on organisms, and decomposers recycle nutrients.

steps.prompt: Arrange the food chain in the direction of energy transfer (producer to predator):
items: Green Grass (Producer)
Grasshopper (Primary Consumer)
Frog (Secondary Consumer)
Snake (Apex Predator)
steps.success: Arrows point in the direction of energy transfer from food to consumer.

questions.text: Which organism is a producer in a grassland food chain?
questions.explanation: Grass makes food through photosynthesis.
questions.feedback: Grass makes food through photosynthesis.

questions.text: What do arrows usually show in a food chain?
options: The direction energy moves from food to consumer
questions.explanation: Arrows point along the direction of energy transfer.
questions.feedback: Arrows point along the direction of energy transfer.

questions.text: Which organism helps break down dead plants and animals?
questions.explanation: Many fungi act as decomposers.
questions.feedback: Many fungi act as decomposers.

questions.text: A vulture eats the remains of a dead animal. What role is it showing?
questions.explanation: Scavengers feed on dead organisms.
questions.feedback: Scavengers feed on dead organisms.

questions.text: If frogs decrease in a grasshopper–frog food chain, what may initially happen to grasshoppers?
options: They may increase because fewer frogs eat them
questions.explanation: With fewer predators, grasshoppers may initially increase.
questions.feedback: With fewer predators, grasshoppers may initially increase.

checkpoints.title: Habitat Balance Trail
checkpoints.npcOpening: Welcome to Habitat Balance Trail! Study the clue first, try the activity, and answer the questions to earn your reward.
checkpoints.lesson: Biotic factors are living parts of an ecosystem; abiotic factors are nonliving conditions such as sunlight, water and temperature. Predators eat prey; competing organisms use limited resources. A scientist measures conditions, records data and considers other possible causes before making conclusions.

miniGame.name: Habitat Map
miniGame.instructions: Drag water, sunlight, tree, fish, soil and frog into living or nonliving categories.

steps.prompt: Habitat Map: classify each pond ecosystem factor as Biotic (Living) or Abiotic (Nonliving).
items: Freshwater fish
Water temperature
Water lily plant
Sunlight intensity
Pond snail
Dissolved minerals in soil
steps.success: Biotic parts are living organisms; abiotic factors are nonliving environmental conditions.

questions.text: Which is an abiotic factor in a pond ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Temperature is a nonliving environmental condition.
questions.feedback: Temperature is a nonliving environmental condition.

questions.text: Which is a biotic factor?
questions.explanation: A water lily is a living organism.
questions.feedback: A water lily is a living organism.

questions.text: What is competition in an ecosystem?
options: Organisms using the same limited resource
questions.explanation: Competition occurs when organisms need limited resources.
questions.feedback: Competition occurs when organisms need limited resources.

questions.text: Which example shows predation?
options: A stone warmed by the Sun
questions.explanation: The snake is a predator consuming prey.
questions.feedback: The snake is a predator consuming prey.

questions.text: A pond has fewer fish than last month. What should students do before claiming pollution caused it?
options: Collect evidence about water conditions and other possible causes
questions.explanation: Scientific conclusions require observations and consideration of alternative explanations.
questions.feedback: Scientific conclusions require observations and consideration of alternative explanations.

checkpoints.title: Machines and Waves Workshop
checkpoints.npcOpening: Welcome to Machines and Waves Workshop! Study the clue first, try the activity, and answer the questions to earn your reward.
checkpoints.lesson: Simple machines such as levers, pulleys and inclined planes can change the size or direction of the force needed. A fair lever test keeps other conditions constant while changing one variable. Waves transfer energy; the material in a water-wave tank mainly oscillates while the disturbance moves through it.

miniGame.name: Build & Test
miniGame.instructions: Choose a ramp or lever to lift a crate and observe ripples in a shallow tub.

steps.prompt: Build & Test: match each tool to its simple machine classification.
items: Slanted ramp used to load a heavy box into a truck
Crowbar pivoting on a fulcrum to pry a rock
Wheel and grooved rope used to hoist a flag
Wheelchair access ramp alongside stairs
steps.success: Simple machines provide mechanical advantage to move loads more easily.

steps.prompt: When ripples pass across a pond, small floating leaves bob up and down. What does this demonstrate?
items: All the water is traveling permanently to the shore
Waves transfer energy outward while particles oscillate in place
Water is solidifying into ice
steps.success: Waves transfer energy across distances without carrying the medium as a whole.

questions.text: Which simple machine is a sloping surface used to raise a box?
questions.explanation: A ramp is an inclined plane.
questions.feedback: A ramp is an inclined plane.

questions.text: What can a lever help a person do?
options: Change the force needed to move a load
questions.explanation: A lever changes the mechanical advantage depending on its arrangement.
questions.feedback: A lever changes the mechanical advantage depending on its arrangement.

questions.text: In a fair test of lever-arm length, what should be kept the same?
questions.explanation: The load must be controlled if lever-arm length is being varied.
questions.feedback: The load must be controlled if lever-arm length is being varied.

questions.text: What is mainly transferred outward by ripples on a water surface?
questions.explanation: Waves transfer energy away from a disturbance.
questions.feedback: Waves transfer energy away from a disturbance.

questions.text: A student sees small floating leaves bob up and down as ripples pass. What is the best conclusion?
options: All pond water flows outward with the ripples
The leaves are being pulled by a magnet
The disturbance moves while the leaves mainly oscillate
questions.explanation: The leaves’ bobbing illustrates wave motion with limited net transport.
questions.feedback: The leaves’ bobbing illustrates wave motion with limited net transport.

missions.title: The Sky and Safety Expedition
missions.story: The village receives unusual sound observations and volcano alerts. Learners use scientific models and official guidance to keep the village safe and explain the night sky.
missions.focus: Longitudinal/transverse waves and sound; volcanoes and preparedness; Philippine seasons, Earth motion and constellations.

finalChallenge.title: Science Expedition Report
finalChallenge.description: Science expedition report: identify wave behavior, choose appropriate volcano-safety decisions and explain Earth rotation using a model.

steps.prompt: Science Expedition Report: classify the wave motions as Transverse or Longitudinal.
items: Ocean surface ripple oscillating up and down
Sound wave traveling through air as pressure pulses
Light traveling through space
Seismic P-wave compressing ground back and forth in travel direction
steps.success: Wave physics accurately categorized!

steps.prompt: When PHIVOLCS raises an alert level and local disaster officials order evacuation, what is the best protocol?
items: Visit the volcanic crater to film the eruption
Promptly follow local evacuation procedures and stay clear of permanent danger zones
Stay indoors without water or emergency supplies
steps.success: Mission 3 complete! You earned the Sky & Safety Badge!

checkpoints.title: Wave Observatory
checkpoints.npcOpening: Welcome to Wave Observatory! Study the clue first, try the activity, and answer the questions to earn your reward.
checkpoints.lesson: Waves transfer energy. In a transverse wave, the motion of the medium is perpendicular to the direction a disturbance travels; in a longitudinal wave, the motion is parallel. Sound in air propagates as compressions and rarefactions. Frequency relates to pitch; amplitude relates to loudness under otherwise comparable conditions.

miniGame.name: Wave Demo
miniGame.instructions: Match rope up-and-down wave and slinky compression wave; compare sound pitch and volume.

steps.prompt: Wave Demo: classify each wave phenomenon by wave type.
items: Rope moving up and down perpendicular to wave travel
Sound wave traveling as compressions and rarefactions in air
Light wave vibrating perpendicular to propagation
Slinky pushed and pulled parallel to wave motion
steps.success: Transverse waves oscillate perpendicular to travel; longitudinal oscillate parallel.

steps.prompt: When the frequency of a sound wave increases, how does its pitch change?
items: It is perceived as lower in pitch
It is perceived as higher in pitch
It instantly turns silent
steps.success: Higher frequency creates a higher musical pitch.

questions.text: Which description fits a transverse wave on a rope?
options: The rope moves up and down while the wave travels along it
The rope travels entirely from one end to the other
The rope disappears as the wave moves
questions.explanation: A transverse disturbance is perpendicular to the direction of wave travel.
questions.feedback: A transverse disturbance is perpendicular to the direction of wave travel.

questions.text: In a longitudinal wave, particles of the medium move mainly how?
questions.explanation: Longitudinal particle motion is parallel to propagation.
questions.feedback: Longitudinal particle motion is parallel to propagation.

questions.text: Sound normally travels through air as what kind of wave?
questions.explanation: Sound in air travels through compressions and rarefactions.
questions.feedback: Sound in air travels through compressions and rarefactions.

questions.text: When sound frequency increases, what generally happens to its pitch?
questions.explanation: Higher frequency corresponds to higher pitch.
questions.feedback: Higher frequency corresponds to higher pitch.

questions.text: With comparable conditions, a larger sound-wave amplitude usually means a sound is perceived as what?
questions.explanation: Amplitude often relates to loudness, not pitch.
questions.feedback: Amplitude often relates to loudness, not pitch.

checkpoints.title: Volcano Safety Center
checkpoints.npcOpening: Welcome to Volcano Safety Center! Study the clue first, try the activity, and answer the questions to earn your reward.
checkpoints.lesson: Volcanoes form where molten rock rises and reaches or approaches Earth’s surface. Eruptions can release lava, ash and gases and create several hazards. PHIVOLCS publishes volcano bulletins and alert guidance in the Philippines. Local authorities may order evacuation; learners should never enter restricted danger zones.

miniGame.name: Safety Board
miniGame.instructions: Classify ashfall, lava, and volcanic gases, then choose safe official-response cards.

steps.prompt: Safety Board: classify each item as Volcanic Material / Hazard vs Official Safety Action.
items: Molten rock flowing at Earth's surface (Lava)
Fine abrasive airborne rock particles (Ashfall)
Monitoring official PHIVOLCS bulletins and alert levels
Promptly evacuating designated restricted danger zones
Closing doors and windows during severe ashfall
steps.success: Safety first! Understanding hazards and following official PHIVOLCS guidance saves lives.

steps.prompt: Which Philippine agency is responsible for official volcano monitoring and alert levels?
items: PAGASA
PHIVOLCS
Department of Agriculture
steps.success: PHIVOLCS provides specialized monitoring for volcanoes, earthquakes, and tsunamis.

questions.text: What is molten rock called after it reaches Earth’s surface?
questions.explanation: Molten rock at the surface is lava.
questions.feedback: Molten rock at the surface is lava.

questions.text: Which hazard can spread fine particles through the air during an eruption?
questions.explanation: Ash can be carried through the atmosphere.
questions.feedback: Ash can be carried through the atmosphere.

questions.text: Which agency provides official Philippine volcano monitoring bulletins?
questions.explanation: PHIVOLCS monitors volcano activity and issues related bulletins.
questions.feedback: PHIVOLCS monitors volcano activity and issues related bulletins.

questions.text: When authorities order evacuation for your location, what is the best response?
options: Wait until ash covers the roof
questions.explanation: Following evacuation orders can reduce exposure to hazards.
questions.feedback: Following evacuation orders can reduce exposure to hazards.

questions.text: Which action is appropriate when volcanic ash is falling and authorities advise staying indoors?
options: Keep windows and doors closed where appropriate
Run outside to collect ash without protection
Approach the volcano to see more clearly
questions.explanation: Limiting ash entry can help protect indoor air, subject to current official guidance.
questions.feedback: Limiting ash entry can help protect indoor air, subject to current official guidance.

checkpoints.title: Night Sky Hill
checkpoints.npcOpening: Welcome to Night Sky Hill! Study the clue first, try the activity, and answer the questions to earn your reward.
checkpoints.lesson: Earth rotates roughly once every day, producing the cycle of day and night. Earth also travels around the Sun. Seasonal differences are related to Earth’s tilted axis and its orbit, while the Philippines commonly describes wet and dry seasons shaped strongly by regional weather and monsoon patterns. Constellations are named apparent star patterns; cultures, including Indigenous communities, have meaningful sky knowledge. A model can help communicate these ideas.

miniGame.name: Sky Match
miniGame.instructions: Rotate an Earth model to show day and night and connect constellation cards to observation notes.

steps.prompt: Sky Match: match Earth's motion to its observable consequence.
items: Roughly 24-hour cycle of day and night
Changing seasonal positions of constellations in the night sky
Sun appearing to rise in the east and set in the west daily
Annual 365.25-day revolution orbit around the Sun
steps.success: Rotation produces day and night; revolution and axial tilt shape seasonal sky changes.

steps.prompt: What is a constellation?
items: A storm cloud inside Earth's atmosphere
A recognizable apparent pattern of stars in the night sky
A single planet orbiting Earth directly
steps.success: Constellations are apparent star patterns seen from Earth with deep cultural and navigation history.

questions.text: What causes the daily cycle of day and night on Earth?
options: The Moon making its own light
questions.explanation: Earth’s rotation alternately exposes places to sunlight.
questions.feedback: Earth’s rotation alternately exposes places to sunlight.

questions.text: Which motion describes Earth traveling around the Sun?
questions.explanation: Earth completes an orbit or revolution around the Sun.
questions.feedback: Earth completes an orbit or revolution around the Sun.

questions.text: Which statement best describes seasons commonly discussed in the Philippines?
options: Wet and dry seasons are strongly influenced by regional weather and monsoons
Seasons happen only because Earth is closer to the Sun
There is no rainfall during the wet season
questions.explanation: Monsoon and regional weather patterns shape Philippine wet and dry seasons.
questions.feedback: Monsoon and regional weather patterns shape Philippine wet and dry seasons.

questions.text: What is a constellation?
options: A group of planets inside Earth
A single star changing its color daily
A recognizable apparent pattern of stars in the sky
questions.explanation: Constellations are apparent patterns of stars as seen from Earth.
questions.feedback: Constellations are apparent patterns of stars as seen from Earth.

questions.text: Why should students study Indigenous knowledge about star patterns respectfully?
options: It has cultural value and records generations of sky observations
It proves every star is the same distance away
It means planets are not real
questions.explanation: Indigenous sky knowledge is culturally meaningful and reflects long-term observation.
questions.feedback: Indigenous sky knowledge is culturally meaningful and reflects long-term observation.
